title: Quick Start
description: Create your first project, place a player and ground in the scene, attach movement logic, and playtest your game in under five minutes.

blocks.content: This guide walks you through building a playable platformer scene from scratch. In a few minutes, you will create a project, add physical entities, wire a movement node, and test your character in the viewport.

items.title: Create a Project
items.desc: Initialize a new game workspace from the **My Projects** dashboard.

items.title: Build the Scene
items.desc: Place a solid ground floor and a dynamic player entity in the viewport.

items.title: Wire Movement
items.desc: Connect **On Tick** to **Platformer Controller** for instant keyboard controls.

items.title: Play & Save
items.desc: Run the live simulation in the editor and save your project to storage.

blocks.content: Start on the **Dashboard** (**My Projects**) to create a new project container.

items: On the **My Projects** page, click **New** next to the heading (or click **Create First Project** if your project list is empty).
In the **New Project** dialog, enter a **Project Name** such as **My First Game** and an optional **Description**.
Click **Create**. The editor opens your new project in the [Editor Overview](interface/editor_overview) workspace.

blocks.content: Next, create a solid floor and a player character using the [Scene Hierarchy](interface/scene_hierarchy), [Scene Viewport](interface/scene_viewport), and [Property Inspector](interface/property_inspector).

items: In the **Scene Hierarchy** on the left, add an entity to your world layer and rename it **Ground**.

With **Ground** selected, click **Add Component** in the **Property Inspector** and add [Shape Renderer](components/renderers/shape_renderer), [Physics Body](components/physics_body), and [Multi-Collider](components/multi_collider).

In the **Property Inspector**, set **Ground**'s [Transform](components/transform) **Size** to **800 x 40**, position it near the bottom of the camera view, and set **Physics Body** **Body Type** to **Static**.
Create a second entity in the **Scene Hierarchy**, rename it **Player**, and position it above **Ground** in the **Scene Viewport**.
In **Player**'s **Physics Body**, keep **Body Type** set to **Dynamic** and enable **Fixed Rotation** so the character stays upright.

blocks.content: Now attach a visual script to **Player** so you can run and jump with the keyboard.

items: Select **Player** in the [Scene Hierarchy](interface/scene_hierarchy), click **Add Component** in the [Property Inspector](interface/property_inspector), and choose [Script Controller](components/script_controller).
In the **Script Controller** section, create or assign a script and open it in the [Graph & Node Concepts](visual_scripting/graph_concepts) editor at the bottom dock.
Right-click the graph canvas, search for [On Tick](node_library/game_lifecycle#node-eventTick), and place it in the graph.
Right-click the canvas again, add [Platformer Controller](node_library/helper_tool#node-platformerController), and connect the white execution pin from **On Tick** into **Platformer Controller**.
Connect the **deltaTime** output pin of **On Tick** to the **deltaTime** input pin of **Platformer Controller**.

blocks.content: Test your scene directly inside the viewport and save your changes to storage.

items: Click **Play** in the top bar. **Player** falls onto **Ground**.
Press **A** and **D** (or the **Left** and **Right** arrow keys) to move horizontally, and press **W** or **Space** to jump.
Click **Stop** in the top bar to return to edit mode, then press **Ctrl + S** to save your project.

blocks.message: Check the status indicator in the top bar: a green dot means your project is synced with storage, while a red dot indicates unsaved changes.
